says: In the tooling, law E3 says allowedDuplicatedPackages appears in tsconfig.base.json only inside one checker override whose include is .agents/** globs alone. The test reads only the first @effect/language-service entry in plugins (line 58, find), and it checks each include glob only for a .agents/ prefix (line 74). So a second checker entry that holds the key, or an include of .agents/../next/**/*.ts, passes.
proof: In a scratch git copy of tsconfig.base.json, .agents/tsconfig.json and the test, run with vitest --root: (1) a second {"name": "@effect/language-service", "allowedDuplicatedPackages": ["effect"]} entry after the first: 1 passed; (2) the override's include set to [".agents/../next/**/*.ts"]: 1 passed. The same copy turns red on next/** added, a second override with no include, a second package name, and a stray tsconfig.extra.json.
cost: A widened allowance could slip in past the law that holds its scope. Whether tsgo honors a second checker entry or a .. glob is not checked.
